W01.title: Create and configure an institution
W01.objective: Create an institution with a unique code and valid address and contact data. Read it by UUID and by code. Replace its security and operational policies, then read both back. The institution ID and policy ownership must stay consistent. Confirm the accepted country-code format, because the description, the example and the validation pattern disagree in the specification.
W01.indicative_calls: 1) POST /institutions (create); 2) GET /institutions/{institutionId} (get); 3) GET /institutions/code/{institutionCode} (getByCode); 4) PUT /institutions/{institutionId}/security-policy (updateSecurity); 5) GET /institutions/{institutionId}/security-policy (getSecurity); 6) PUT /institutions/{institutionId}/operational-policy (updateOperational); 7) GET /institutions/{institutionId}/operational-policy (getOperational); 8) POST /institutions/{institutionId}/actions/update (update)
W01.note: The institution used for the run is the CMS institution mapped to the Switch test institution; it is created or refreshed by fixture 01.1. Create-path validation (duplicate code, invalid code, invalid country) is covered by 32.4 to 32.6. With card issuance disabled in the operational policy, a new issuance is refused at submission (HTTP 422) and existing cards keep working (26.4 to 26.10).

W03.title: Configure BIN and BIN range
W03.objective: Create a 6 or 8 digit BIN for RUPAY. Read it, replace its mutable configuration, add a non-overlapping same-prefix BIN range, activate the range and verify capacity. Confirm an overlapping range is rejected. Two items to settle here: binType currently offers CREDIT only, so confirm whether debit BINs are in scope, and confirm the accepted format of effectiveFrom, which is typed as a date but shown with a time.
W03.indicative_calls: 1) POST /institutions/{institutionId}/bins (createBin); 2) GET /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId} (getBin); 3) PUT /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId} (updateBin); 4) POST /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId}/ranges (createRange); 5) POST /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId}/ranges/{rangeId}/actions/update (updateRange); 6) GET /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId}/ranges/{rangeId} (getRange)
W03.note: BINs are issued on the VISA network in this environment; RUPAY-specific BIN configuration was not available. 6-digit and 8-digit BINs, range activation, capacity, overlap rejection, optimistic locking and immutable-field protection were verified.

W04.title: Configure HSM keys for the BIN
W04.objective: Prepare compatible PVK ,CVK, and ZPK keys, activate them, assign them to the BIN for the required PIN and CVV purposes and activate each assignment. HSM-generated PIN issuance requires active BIN PVK,CVK and ZPK assignments, so confirm PIN operations are refused until both are active.
W04.indicative_calls: 1) Create each key with POST /institutions/{institutionId}/hsm-keys or POST /institutions/{institutionId}/hsm-keys/registrations; 2) PUT /institutions/{institutionId}/hsm-keys/{keyId}/status for each key; 3) POST /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId}/hsm-key-assignments for each purpose; 4) PUT /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId}/hsm-key-assignments/{assignmentId}/status for each assignment; 5) GET /institutions/{institutionId}/bins/{binId}/hsm-key-assignments
W04.status_note: PVK and ZPK assignments confirmed active on 20 October 2026
W04.note: CVV (CVK) and EMV key-derivation assignments were generated, activated and assigned on 16 October. On 20 October, samplers 05.17 to 05.25 generated a BIN PVK, assigned it for PIN generation, generated an institution ZPK, assigned it to the BIN for PIN-block encryption, and confirmed both assignments are ACTIVE. The check rows below remain the 16 October evidence.

W19.title: Replace a damaged or expired card
W19.objective: Use a physical-capable card and the exact active reason policy. Request replacement with the allowed PAN, shipping and production choices. Verify the resolved PAN strategy, the old and new card states and the production linkage. The important check is at the Switch: confirm the old card stops authorising in the way the policy says it should, whether that is immediately, on activation of the new card, or on first use. If the request stops at pending approval, record that state and stop there.

W25.title: Run the complete lifecycle smoke test
W25.objective: Run one fresh ordered lifecycle: institution, policies, HSM and data keys, BIN, range and key assignment, product, version, policies, profiles and design, activation, issuance, control change, limit change, PIN operation, replacement or hot-listing, and one authorisation. Read state after every write. This becomes the regression smoke test for future releases and major changes.
W25.indicative_calls: 1) Run the ordered API calls in workflows 1 to 8; 2) Run one issuance sequence from workflows 9 to 13; 3) GET /institutions/{institutionId}/cards/{cardId}; 4) Run the GET, PUT, GET sequences in workflows 14 and 15; 5) Run the PIN APIs in workflow 16 where PIN is enabled; 6) Run either the hot-list or replacement APIs in workflows 17 to 19 on an eligible card; 7) Run workflow 26 and one decline from workflow 35; 8) Finish with GET /institutions/{institutionId}/cards (listCardsV2) and direct GETs for all resulting resources
W25.note: The ordered lifecycle is executed as the shared bootstrap and the ordered thread groups of the plan; each leg below points at the checks that prove it. The authorisation leg requires the NPCI simulator and is outside this run.

W28.status_note: Reserved for later execution; no matching attempt in this supplied NPCI log.

W30.objective: Send an ATM cash withdrawal with an online PIN block. Confirm approval, PIN verification under the BIN ZPK, and which control and limit were applied. W32.objective: Send one international POS purchase and one international e-commerce transaction. Confirm the international controls and international limits were applied and not the domestic ones.
W32.indicative_calls: 1) GET the card controls; 2) Send both transactions from the NPCI simulator; 3) Read the Switch authorisation records

W33.title: Refund or credit to the card

W33.indicative_calls: 1) Send the refund from the NPCI simulator; 2) Read the Switch authorisation record; 3) Read the available balance in accounting

W34.title: Balance enquiry
W34.objective: Send a balance enquiry. Confirm the balance returned matches what accounting holds, and that no hold is created.
W34.indicative_calls: 1) Send the balance enquiry from the NPCI simulator; 2) Read the Switch record; 3) Compare against the accounting balance
W34.status_note: Selected older transaction evidence is included. The complete Table 3 scenario, including historical controls and accounting effects, is not fully verified.

W35.title: Decline cases
W35.objective: Prove each decline separately and record the response code for each: channel disabled, per-transaction limit exceeded, card hot-listed, card expired, wrong PIN, wrong CVV. Each of these is the end-to-end proof for workflows 14, 15, 16 and 17. Change the control or limit in CMS first, then send the transaction, and confirm the outcome changes.
W35.indicative_calls: 1) Change the relevant control, limit or card status in CMS; 2) Confirm the Switch acknowledged the new version; 3) Send the matching transaction from the NPCI simulator; 4) Read the Switch authorisation record and the decline reason
W35.status_note: Selected older transaction evidence is included. The complete Table 3 scenario, including historical controls and accounting effects, is not fully verified.
W35.cms_preconditions_verified: Control, limit, hot-list and PIN changes in CMS (W14–W17)

W36.title: Pre-authorisation creates a hold
W36.objective: Send a pre-authorisation with DE-25 = 55, an eligible MCC, and sufficient funds. Confirm the Switch identifies it as pre-authorisation and accounting reserves the authorised amount. Available balance decreases by that amount, with no settled debit at this stage.
W36.indicative_calls: 1) Record the available balance in accounting; 2) Send the pre-authorisation from the NPCI simulator using an eligible MCC, such as 7011; 3) Verify the approval and pre-authorisation classification in the Switch record; 4) Verify the linked accounting hold and the reduced available balance.
W36.status_note: Selected older transaction evidence is included. The complete Table 3 scenario, including historical controls and accounting effects, is not fully verified.

W37.title: Cancellation releases the pre-authorisation hold
W37.objective: Cancel an approved pre-authorisation before presentment. Confirm the reversal is linked to the original authorisation, the corresponding hold is fully released in accounting, and available balance is restored without a settled debit.
W37.indicative_calls: 1) Create an approved pre-authorisation and record its reference, hold amount, and available balance; 2) Send a matching cancellation/reversal from the NPCI simulator; 3) Verify the Switch reversal record and its link to the original authorisation; 4) Verify accounting releases the hold and increases available balance by the released amount.
W37.status_note: Selected older transaction evidence is included. The complete Table 3 scenario, including historical controls and accounting effects, is not fully verified.

W38.title: Timely final presentment settles the authorised transaction
W38.objective: Present the final amount by Day 6, with Day 0 being the authorisation date. Run once for an amount equal to the hold and once for a lower amount. Confirm accounting posts only the final amount, consumes/releases the original hold, and releases any unused portion without reducing available balance twice. It should be noted that Switch doesn’t age and expire authorisations - that has to be managed by the accounting system. If need be read already shared documents - Pre-auth transactions: Accounting tracks expiry and releases the hold on Day 7 if no presentment was received by Day 6. Hold and its expiry is an accounting-owned lifecycle check
W38.indicative_calls: 1) Create an approved pre-authorisation and record its accounting hold; 2) Submit a matching presentment through the clearing/settlement test flow by Day 6; 3) Verify it is matched to the original pre-authorisation; 4) Verify the posted amount, removal of the hold, and final available balance; 5) Repeat with a lower final amount and verify the unused portion becomes available.
W38.status_note: Reserved for later execution; no matching attempt in this supplied NPCI log.

W39.title: Full authorisation reversal
W39.objective: Reverse an authorisation in full. Confirm the hold is released completely and the available balance returns to its prior value.
W39.indicative_calls: 1) Read the hold and balance; 2) Send the reversal from the NPCI simulator; 3) Read the hold and balance again
W39.status_note: Selected older transaction evidence is included. The complete Table 3 scenario, including historical controls and accounting effects, is not fully verified.

W40.title: Partial reversal
W40.objective: Reverse part of an authorisation. Confirm the hold is reduced by the reversed amount and the remainder stays in place.
W40.indicative_calls: 1) Read the hold and balance; 2) Send the partial reversal from the NPCI simulator; 3) Read the hold and balance again
W40.status_note: Reserved for later execution; no matching attempt in this supplied NPCI log.

W41.title: Timeout reversal
W41.objective: Simulate no issuer response, then send the timeout reversal. Confirm no orphan hold is left and the balance is correct. Also send a duplicate reversal and confirm it does not release the hold twice.
W41.indicative_calls: 1) Force a timeout at the simulator; 2) Send the reversal; 3) Read the hold and balance; 4) Send the same reversal again and read both once more
W41.status_note: Reserved for later execution; no matching attempt in this supplied NPCI log.

W42.title: Authorisation completion or advice
W42.objective: Send a completion or advice against a pre-authorisation. Confirm the hold is adjusted to the final amount and the record is linked to the original authorisation.
W42.indicative_calls: 1) Read the hold; 2) Send the completion from the NPCI simulator; 3) Read the hold and the linked authorisation record
W42.status_note: Reserved for later execution; no matching attempt in this supplied NPCI log.

W43.title: Hold expiry with no clearing
W43.objective: Leave an authorisation with no clearing until the agreed hold period passes. Confirm the hold is released automatically by the accounting system in the accounting system, the balance is restored, and the expiry is reported. Record the hold period used for each transaction classification. Switch will not track the expiry of auth, Recon also will not age the auth and advise for its expiry, this should be handled within the accounting system.

findings.title: Activating the successor BIN key assignment fails with HTTP 500
findings.expected: The successor assignment becomes ACTIVE and the prior assignment moves to VERIFY_ONLY in one operation; new issuance uses the successor key.
findings.observed: Rotation of the BIN CVK itself succeeded: the successor key was registered with lineage, activated, and the prior key moved to DECRYPT_ONLY (41.37b to 41.38a). Activating the successor BIN key assignment returned HTTP 500 INTERNAL_ERROR; the read-back shows the prior assignment still ACTIVE and the successor still PENDING_APPROVAL. Post-rotation issuance (41.60 to 41.62) was therefore not executed, and cards issued before the attempt kept their original key reference (41.65).

findings.title: Status naming for a rotated key differs from the scenario wording
findings.expected: Agree the terminology in the API specification; behaviour at key level is otherwise as described.
findings.observed: After successor activation the prior key reports status DECRYPT_ONLY at key level; VERIFY_ONLY is the status used at BIN key-assignment level. The scenario text uses VERIFY_ONLY for both.

findings.title: Hot-list endpoint not exercisable with the test client
findings.expected: Execute W17 with cardholder-channel and operations tokens that carry the hot-list permission.
findings.observed: All hot-list calls were refused with HTTP 403 because the test client does not hold the hot-list permission. The permission gate itself behaves correctly; the hot-list business flow (prior status, BLOCKED status, event ID, caller type from token) was not exercised.

findings.title: Tenant isolation not provable with a platform-scoped client
findings.expected: Provide a second, institution-scoped client to prove tenant isolation.
findings.observed: The plan authenticates with a platform-scoped client, so a cross-tenant read could not be attempted. Unknown-institution and unknown-card reads return 404 without leaking data (23.5, 23.10).

redaction.policy: Bearer tokens, client secrets, key material (key blocks and key check values), PIN blocks, PIN decimalisation tables and full PANs are replaced by [REDACTED]; any other 16-19 digit number except BIN range bounds is masked to its first six and last four digits. PANs returned by the API are already masked by the product.

scenarios.title: Domestic retail purchase at POS, contact chip
evidence_summary: Three domestic POS chip purchase attempts for INR 1 each. Two responses are approved 00 and one is FORMAT_ERROR 30 after mandatory EMV tag 9F02 was omitted.
Database fields record PURCHASE, source_channel POS, DE19=356, DE22=051 and DE25=00.
limitations: Applied card control and limit configuration, hold records and before-and-after available balances are not independently established. The format-error decline does not cover any of the six enumerated W35 decline cases.

scenarios.title: Domestic contactless below the CVM limit
Domestic contactless above the CVM limit
Domestic ATM cash withdrawal with online PIN
Refund or credit to the card
Pre-authorisation creates a hold
evidence_summary: Three PREAUTH attempts with DE25=55, amounts INR 80, 90 and 70, and MCCs 7011, 8062 and 4121 respectively. All have saved response 00 and primary transaction status SUCCESS.
The Switch logs five accounting authorisation calls across the two approved purchases and three pre-authorisations.
limitations: An accounting-simulator approval is recorded, but creation of a hold and the reduction in available balance are unverified. MCC eligibility and sufficient-funds accounting are not independently proved.

scenarios.title: Timely final presentment settles the authorised transaction
Full authorisation reversal
evidence_summary: One INR 1 reversal of the INR 1 purchase under RRN 628920767460. DE90 identifies original MTI 0100, STAN 767460 and transmission date-time 1016145803.
The saved reversal response is MTI 0430, DE39=00, DE38=KCDJWK. Both the 0420 primary transaction row and the 0430 helper transaction row show FAILED.
limitations: The log approves the reversal in application mode. Full accounting hold release and restoration of available balance are unverified, so the complete scenario is not marked passed.

findings.title: Reversal response and transaction status disagree
findings.observed: RRN 628920767460 has a saved 0430 response 00, while its primary 0420 and helper 0430 transaction rows are FAILED. The log approves in application mode. Accounting release is unverified.

findings.title: Declined purchase remains pending in the transaction table
findings.observed: RRN 628920020523 has a saved 0110 response 30 for FORMAT_ERROR after missing EMV tag 9F02, while its primary transaction row remains PENDING.

findings.title: Database source and accounting scope
findings.observed: The logged database host 192.168.158.36 timed out. Read-only extraction used local PostgreSQL 127.0.0.1 with exact RRN, register ID, ISO transaction ID and timestamp matches. This does not establish that the two database endpoints are identical. No hold, posting or available-balance proof was retrieved.

findings.title: Decline notification returns HTTP 401
findings.observed: The malformed purchase decline triggered a CMS transaction-declined notification which returned HTTP 401. The Switch response remains 30; successful CMS notification processing is unverified.

limitations: Pasted file is a switch application log, not an NPCI simulator packet capture. Full simulator ISO messages and full switch/CMS HTTP bodies do not appear.
Request fields reconstructed from MAC inputs are explicitly labelled and are not full original payloads.
Six unique RRNs map to seven transaction attempts because reversal and original purchase share one RRN.
Application approval is distinct from CMS posting or reversal; database evidence is required.

Full ordinary stored transaction columns and saved response fields are included, with sensitive authentication and card data redacted. Database response_message values are empty, so a complete original wire response cannot be recovered from these sources.
No direct access to the external accounting simulator database was available. Zero RRN matches in queried CMS/clearing event tables do not prove absence from all systems.

scenarios.title: Domestic retail purchase at POS, contact chip
scenarios.notes: Domestic POS chip fields are present; applied controls/limits and accounting hold effects are not retained as transaction history.

scenarios.title: Domestic contactless below the CVM limit
scenarios.notes: Eight domestic contactless purchase candidates exist, shared with W28. Historical CVM thresholds and PIN/CVM evidence are absent, so none can be assigned specifically to below-CVM.

scenarios.title: Domestic contactless above the CVM limit
scenarios.notes: The same eight contactless purchase candidates apply. Stored PIN blocks and CVM results are absent; this does not prove that PIN was absent on the original request. Above-CVM/PIN verification cannot be assigned.

scenarios.title: Domestic e-commerce, card not present
scenarios.notes: No retained record matches the ECOMMERCE fields in the available Switch rules. DE22=801 is PURCHASE_FALLBACK, not e-commerce. Missing legacy fields mean absence of a match does not prove no e-commerce test was ever run.

scenarios.title: Domestic ATM cash withdrawal with online PIN
scenarios.notes: Requires processing code 010000, ATM01 channel tag, acquiring country356 and MCC6011. Online PIN verification, the historical applied limit and accounting debit/hold effects are not proved.

scenarios.title: International POS and international e-commerce
scenarios.notes: International POS component only. No identifiable international e-commerce record; the combined scenario is not complete.

scenarios.title: Refund or credit to the card
scenarios.notes: Refund processing code 200000 is retained in 47 request records, all sharing RRN 516015123456 across 31 distinct composite request keys. None has an exact saved-response match. These are not 47 distinct certification test cases. Credit accounting direction and balance effects are unverified. Money-load codes 28/29 are separately reported, not silently counted as refunds.

scenarios.title: Balance enquiry
scenarios.notes: Balance-enquiry processing code310000 is retained. Returned balances and accounting equality/no-hold requirements are not established by this count.

scenarios.title: Decline cases
scenarios.notes: 113 linked response 55 wrong-PIN records and two linked response 61 limit records. These include different transaction types, including 18 failed PIN-change requests. Seven more response 61 rows have no exact request-key match. Generic 05 cannot identify wrong CVV; codes 58/62 do not prove a CMS channel-disable or hot-list test. No expired/lost/stolen-specific responses were found.

scenarios.title: Pre-authorisation creates a hold
scenarios.notes: One older approved INR 75 pre-authorisation, RRN 609812914133, on 8 April 2026. Accounting hold creation is unverified.

scenarios.title: Cancellation releases the pre-authorisation hold
scenarios.notes: One cancellation request links exactly by DE90 and anonymous card identity to the approved INR 75 pre-authorisation. Reversal response 96 is a failure; release of the hold was not demonstrated.

scenarios.title: Timely final presentment settles the authorised transaction
scenarios.notes: Switch history does not establish clearing presentment timing, posting, hold consumption or release. No case counted.

scenarios.title: Full authorisation reversal
scenarios.notes: Positive full-amount reversals linked by DE90+card identity to approved original debit authorisations. Includes one W37 pre-authorisation cancellation. Saved reversal codes and original codes are retained; accounting release is unverified.

scenarios.title: Partial reversal
scenarios.notes: All127 uniquely linked older reversals repeat the original amount. No positive reversal amount lower than the original and no DE95 replacement amount was found.

scenarios.title: Timeout reversal
scenarios.notes: Generic reversal records exist, but timeout reason and duplicate-release behaviour are not retained. No request can be identified confidently as this exact timeout scenario.

scenarios.title: Authorisation completion or advice
scenarios.notes: No0120/0220 completion/advice request or retained completion function/condition evidence found.

scenarios.title: Hold expiry with no clearing
scenarios.notes: Hold expiry belongs to accounting under the reference. It cannot be established from the inspected Switch history.

method: Exclude the eight exact primary/helper row IDs from the latest supplied run; retain all other legacy request rows, including undated records, explicitly flagged.
Request record counts are not unique certification test cases:71 records repeat a composite request key. No authoritative certification case ID is stored.
Saved responses join on exact MTI+DE7+RRN composite ISO transaction identifier. Numeric register IDs belong to a different identifier family.
Reversal links use DE90 from the primary request OR saved response, match original MTI/STAN/transmission date-time and anonymous same-card group, and require exactly one original.
Current available RuPay rule definitions from the local falcon-switch-core1.0.58 image interpret retained ISO fields; this is not a claim that every historical version derived the same type.
Only response codes55 and61 are counted as specific W35 signals. Other codes are retained separately and not forced into unsupported reasons.
Counts establish historical transaction evidence only; none proves all document requirements, controls, CVM/PIN checks, accounting holds, balances, settlement or expiry.
W01-W25 are CMS setup/lifecycle workflows and are outside a payment-history count. Network PIN-change history related to W16 is reported separately.
